questions.q:
Match List - I with List - II:
List - I (Element-Atomic number): (a) Ra - 88 (b) Ga - 31 (c) W - 74 (d) Pd - 46
List - II (Position in periodic table): (i) 4$^{th}$ period, 13$^{th}$ group (ii) 6$^{th}$ period, 6$^{th}$ group (iii) 5$^{th}$ period, 10$^{th}$ group (iv) 7$^{th}$ period, 2$^{nd}$ group
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: a - iv, b - i, c - ii, d - iii
a - i, b - ii, c - iii, d - iv
a - iv, b - ii, c - iii, d - i
a - iii, b - iv, c - i, d - ii
questions.explanation: Ra (Z=88) is in period 7, group 2; Ga (Z=31) is in period 4, group 13; W (Z=74) is in period 6, group 6; Pd (Z=46) is in period 5, group 10 — matching a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii.

questions.q: Given below are the atomic masses of the elements: Li=7, Na=23, Cl=35.5, K=39, Ca=40, Br=80, Sr=88, I=127, Ba=137 (g mol$^{-1}$). Which of the following doesn't form a triad?
questions.explanation: In a Dobereiner triad the atomic mass of the middle element is the average of the other two; this holds for Li-Na-K, Ba-Sr-Ca and Cl-Br-I, but not for Cl, K, Ca.

questions.q: The correct order of first ionisation enthalpy of given elements is
questions.explanation: First ionisation enthalpy generally increases across period 2, but Be (fully-filled 2s$^2$) and B (2s$^2$2p$^1$) show an anomaly since boron's electron is lost from a higher-energy p-orbital; the correct order is Li < B < Be < C.

questions.q: A pair of amphoteric oxides is
questions.explanation: BeO and ZnO both react with acids as well as bases, making them amphoteric oxides; Li$_2$O and MgO are basic oxides.

questions.q: Elements X, Y and Z have atomic numbers 19, 37 and 55 respectively. Which of the following statements is true about them?
options: Z would have the highest ionization potential.
Their ionization potential would increase with increasing atomic number.
Y would have the highest ionization potential.
Y would have an ionization potential between those of X and Z.
questions.explanation: X, Y, Z are K, Rb, Cs (alkali metals). Ionization potential decreases down the group (K > Rb > Cs), so Y (Rb) lies between X (K) and Z (Cs).

questions.q: Amphoteric oxide among the following
questions.explanation: BeO is amphoteric because of the diagonal relationship of Be with Al, so it reacts with both acids and bases.

questions.q: The third ionisation enthalpy is highest in
questions.explanation: Alkaline earth metals have a stable +2 (noble gas-like) configuration; removing a third electron from this stable ion requires very high energy.

questions.q: The last element of the p-block in 6$^{th}$ period is represented by the outer most electronic configuration:
questions.explanation: The last p-block element of period 6 is radon (Z=86), whose configuration is [Xe]4f$^{14}$5d$^{10}$6s$^2$6p$^6$.

questions.q: The first ionization enthalpy of the following elements are in the order:
questions.explanation: Ionization enthalpy increases across a period and decreases down a group; among C, N, Si, P the correct increasing order is Si < P < C < N (N has extra stability from a half-filled 2p subshell).

questions.q: Which of the following is the correct order of radius ?
questions.explanation: H$^-$ has an extra electron so it is the largest, neutral H is smaller, and H$^+$ (a bare proton) is essentially a point charge, the smallest.

questions.q: The electronegativities of C, N, Si and P are in the order of
questions.explanation: Electronegativity increases across a period and decreases down a group, giving Si < P < C < N.

questions.q: For one of the element various successive ionization enthalpies (in kJ mol$^{-1}$) are given below: I.E. 1st=577.5, 2nd=1810, 3rd=2750, 4th=11,580, 5th=14,820. The element is
questions.explanation: The very large jump between the 3rd and 4th ionization enthalpies shows only 3 valence electrons, and the magnitude of IE$_1$ (577.5 kJ/mol) matches aluminium.

questions.q: The correct arrangement for the ions in the increasing order of their radii is
questions.explanation: Ca$^{2+}$ (isoelectronic with Ar, smallest among these, most charge/nuclear pull) < K$^+$ (same isoelectronic series, less charge) < S$^{2-}$ (isoelectronic with Ar but with extra electrons, largest); this gives the correct increasing radii order.

questions.q: For the properties mentioned, the correct trend for the different species is in
options: first ionization enthalpy – B > Al > Tl
inert pair effect – Al > Ga > In
strength as Lewis acid – BCl$_3$ > AlCl$_3$ > GaCl$_3$
questions.explanation: Lewis acid strength of the group 13 trichlorides decreases down the group as BCl$_3$ > AlCl$_3$ > GaCl$_3$ (boron's small size gives the best orbital overlap for accepting a lone pair despite p$\pi$-p$\pi$ back-bonding). The other options misstate their trends: first IE is actually B > Tl > Al; oxidising power is Tl$^{3+}$ > In$^{3+}$ > Al$^{3+}$ (inert pair effect); inert pair effect increases down the group (In > Ga > Al), not decreases.

questions.q: Which one of the following sets of ions represents the collection of isoelectronic species ?
questions.explanation: K$^+$, Ca$^{2+}$, Sc$^{3+}$ and Cl$^-$ all have 18 electrons, making them isoelectronic.

questions.q: The correct order of electronegativities of N, O, F & P is
questions.explanation: Electronegativity increases across a period and decreases down a group: F(4.0) > O(3.5) > N(3.0) > P(2.1).

questions.q: The correct order of ionisation energy of C, N, O & F is
questions.explanation: Ionisation energies: C≈1086, O≈1314, N≈1402, F≈1681 kJ/mol. N has extra stability from a half-filled 2p$^3$ configuration, raising its IE above O's, giving the order C < O < N < F.

questions.q: Generally, the first ionization energy increases along a period. But there are some exceptions. The one which is NOT an exception is ..............
questions.explanation: Ionization energy increases normally from Na to Mg; Be-B, N-O and Mg-Al are all exceptions to the normal trend due to stable filled or half-filled subshells.

questions.q: Generally, the first ionization energy increases along a period. But there are some exceptions. One which is NOT an exception is ...............
questions.explanation: Be-B, N-O and Mg-Al are known exceptions (due to stable filled/half-filled subshells); Na to Mg follows the normal increasing trend.

questions.q: For alkali metals, which one of the following trends is INCORRECT?
options: Ionization energy : Li > Na > K > Rb
Hydration energy : Li > Na > K > Rb
Atomic size : Li < Na < K < Rb
questions.explanation: Density does not increase smoothly down the group; potassium is actually less dense than sodium, so 'Li < Na < K < Rb' is incorrect.

questions.q: The correct order of ionisation energy of C, N, O, F is
questions.explanation: N has extra stability from a half-filled 2p$^3$ subshell, so its ionisation energy exceeds O's, giving C < O < N < F.

questions.q: The oxide of an element whose electronic configuration is 1s$^2$ 2s$^2$ 2p$^6$ 3s$^1$ is
questions.explanation: The configuration is of sodium (Na); Na$_2$O, an alkali metal oxide, is basic.
